record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
record.original_question: Let S be a topological inverse semigroup, let E(S) be the subsemigroup of idempotents of S, and let H = {H(e) | e in E(S)} be the family of maximal subgroups of S. Given topological properties P_1 and P_2, if E(S) has property P_1 and each maximal subgroup H(e) has property P_2, what topological properties must the whole semigroup S have?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a topological inverse semigroup, that is, a Hausdorff topological space equipped with a continuous associative multiplication $S\times S\to S$ such that every element $s\in S$ has a unique inverse $s^{-1}$ satisfying $ss^{-1}s=s$ and $s^{-1}ss^{-1}=s^{-1}$, with the inversion map $s\mapsto s^{-1}$ continuous. Let
$$E(S)=\{e\in S:e^2=e\}$$
be the subsemigroup of idempotents of $S$, endowed with the subspace topology, and for each $e\in E(S)$ let
$$H(e)=\{s\in S:ss^{-1}=s^{-1}s=e,\ \exists\,t\in S\text{ with }st=ts=e\}$$
denote the maximal subgroup of $S$ at $e$, again with the subspace topology. The family $\mathcal{H}=\{H(e):e\in E(S)\}$ partitions the set of group-like elements of $S$.

Given two topological properties $P_1$ and $P_2$ (for example: compactness, local compactness, metrizability, separability, Lindelöf property, $\sigma$-compactness, paracompactness, completeness, pseudocompactness, countable tightness, etc.), determine which topological properties $Q$ must necessarily hold for $S$ under the assumption that $E(S)$ has property $P_1$ and every maximal subgroup $H(e)$, $e\in E(S)$, has property $P_2$.

More precisely: characterize, for each pair $(P_1,P_2)$, the strongest topological property $Q=Q(P_1,P_2)$ such that whenever $E(S)$ satisfies $P_1$ and all $H(e)$ satisfy $P_2$, the topological inverse semigroup $S$ must satisfy $Q$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad meta-problem asking, for arbitrary pairs of topological properties $(P_1,P_2)$, what is inherited by a topological inverse semigroup $S$ from its idempotent subsemigroup $E(S)$ and its maximal subgroups $H(e)$. Searches reveal active research on related special cases (e.g., locally compact shift-continuous topologies on simple inverse $\omega$-semigroups with compact maximal subgroups), but no comprehensive resolution of the general transfer problem. The overall status appears open/unresolved in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: On semitopological simple inverse ω-semigroups with compact maximal subgroups
status_evidence.snippet: Hausdorff locally compact shift-continuous topology on simple inverse semitopological ω-semigroups with compact maximal subgroups...
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses special cases of how properties of maximal subgroups transfer to the whole inverse semigroup, indicating the general problem remains a topic of ongoing investigation.

status_evidence.title: A topological approach to inverse and regular semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Topological approach to inverse semigroups via ordered groupoids.
status_evidence.claim: General structure theory exists but does not give a uniform answer to which properties of S follow from properties of E(S) and the H(e).
